newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Global One open minded on seeking local partners.
newsitem.headline: Global One open minded on seeking local partners.

text.p: Global One, the telecoms venture of Deutsche Telekom AG, France Telecom and Sprint Corp of the U.S., said it had an open mind about partnerships with local operators to help it expand.

"We don't exclude the fact that we may have local partners. But we must have sufficient control so that they work according to our rules," Gerard Simonet, the head of Global One's pan-European operator unit, said on Wednesday.
"It is easier to drive a company you own than one you don't," he added. "If we felt we were courting a risk that our clients would get a downgraded service we would say no."
Simonet was speaking at a presentation organised by the Brussels Telecommunications Forum.
Set up at the end of January, Global One offers advanced voice and data services for businesses, carriers and consumers. It also offers calling card services for travellers.
"Growth is a two-digit figure. Everything is improving in line with the business plan," Simonet said, declining to give details or comment on profitability.
The venture, which received approval from the European Commission on July 17, employs about 3,000 people and estimates 1996 revenues will total $800 million.
Simonet said he did not envisage a public offering of Global One stock in the future, saying it was unnecessary as its parents would all be bourse-listed.
